answer: Heartbeat registry: an agent only counts as a voter after it posts a signed heartbeat every 6 hours for 30 days, and each heartbeat costs 0.5 POA in fees. One identity therefore pays 0.5 x 4 x 30 = 60 POA; ten fakes pay 600 POA, and a hundred pay 6000. Real work is cheap by comparison: an oasis agent serving actual requests earns nectar-like fees that cover its heartbeats. Auditors sample 5 percent of heartbeats and slash 20 POA from identities whose onyx-signed pings share one machine fingerprint. The limit: a rich attacker can still pay, so the registry only raises price.
